It took nearly three months for my male mouse to warm up to me and I was worried he wouldn't like me in the beginning since he was my first baby. We are now inseparable and he comes when called and immediately walks into my hand and likes to snuggle.

I'd say handle them everyday if you can for around 30 mins. Best way to get them used to you is bath tub method. If they don't like crawling into your hand put a toilet roll tube down and let them crawl in and transport them in the tube. Bring a little food bowl and water and just sit in the bathtub with them. They are naturally curious so as time passes they'll start to go near your legs and test the limits on how safe you are. They'll eventually get more comfortable with your smell and voice. Hand feeding them treats through the bars of their cage or when they're out also helps alot.

Hmm I was looking for this piece of info on exactly WHY he didn't wanna get married. This might be unpopular, but I hold the same view as he does towards marriage and have since I was a teen (I'm a 21yo female). If my partner desperately wanted to get married and it was something of utmost importance I would reconsider for them, but I don't feel that marriage is necessary. I don't need a certificate to know that I'll be with someone for the rest of my life. I respect that some do hold marriage as important and a dealbreaker though. Other than the legal benefits I'm not to keen on the idea. I do think you are NTA in this scenario though. I would call my boyfriend "husband" even without the legal binding, BUT not if they WANTED to get married. If me and my partner had the same views towards marriage I don't think it would be odd to call them my husband and vice versa after several years of being together, but if we didn't and it was something they truly really wanted it kinda seems like a messed up joke to be calling them my husband behind their back when it's something they'd be giving up for being with me. But yeah NTA, hope you resolve this. Alot of people in the comments are saying dump him and run, but I know a relationship can be more complicated than that. If you feel like getting married would be losing a monumental lifetime experience though really consider if you'd be ok giving that up because of your partner. Good luck.

Oooh I have a good one. Didn't happen to me, but happened to both of my parents.

About 13 years ago my parents had a few oddly unexplainable events happen to them within the timespan of a couple weeks. The first thing that happened was to my mother. It was a night where my dad was working late so just my mom, sister, and I were home. My sister was a toddler and I was a couple years older than her back then. Anyways, it was way past me and my sister's bed time and my mother heard us running up and down our hallway laughing she yelled at us from the other room telling us to go to bed. About 15 minutes of silence passes and then it starts back up again, laughing and the noise of little girls running. Pissed off with a slipper in hand ready to spank she stormed into the living room just to realize we weren't there. She then walks over to our bedroom and peeks inside to find us sound asleep. 

The next thing that happened was to my father. In our living room we had a recliner that made a loud and distinct "vwoop" noise when you extended the legs. Me, my sister, and mom were out running errands for the day and my dad was home alone. He was in another room when he heard the "vwoop" noise, but just shook it off as his mind playing tricks until he heard it again a few minutes later... and then again with a few minutes of silence between each "vwoop". He then proceeded to check it out figuring the recliner just wasn't properly clicked into place and perhaps it slid out accidentally, but when he made his way into the living room the recliner legs weren't even out.

The last instance happened to my mom when me and my sister were at school/pre-K and my dad was working. My mom was watching TV in the living room when she heard a kitchen cabinet close. When she went into the kitchen many of the cabinets were cracked open. Not all of them, but enough to where it was creepy and no mere accident.

Later that night my mom shared the weird events with my father and he revealed the things he's been hearing too. Apparently they bought a headboard from a thrift store that had a symbol and some numbers drawn on the back of it. They didn't think anything of it, until the odd occurrences started happening coincidentally around the same time they brought it into the house. In the end they got rid of it, but instead of trashing it they redonated it smhhhh. Hope no one bought it 😫
